Plotting in map form¶

In [2]:
# --- 1. Load and Prepare ---
master_df = pd.read_csv("../data/preprocessed/barcelona/barcelona_master_dataframe.csv")
master_df['geometry'] = master_df['geometry'].apply(wkt.loads)

# Create GeoDataFrame & Reproject
master_gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(master_df, geometry='geometry', crs='epsg:25831')
master_gdf = master_gdf.to_crs(epsg=4326)

# Filter for latest year
target_year = 2015
latest_year_gdf = master_gdf[master_gdf['year'] == target_year]

# --- 2. Create the Grid Plot ---
plots = {
    'median_household_income': {'title': 'Median Household Income', 'cmap': 'viridis'},
    'median_price_per_m2': {'title': 'Median Price (€/m²)', 'cmap': 'plasma'}, # <--- The one with imputation
    'pct_young_adults': {'title': '% Young Adults', 'cmap': 'cividis'},
    'population_density': {'title': 'Population Density', 'cmap': 'inferno'}
}

fig, axes = plt.subplots(nrows=2, ncols=2, figsize=(10, 10))
axes = axes.flatten()

for i, (column, plot_info) in enumerate(plots.items()):
    ax = axes[i]
    
    # A. Base Plot (All Data)
    latest_year_gdf.plot(
        column=column,
        ax=ax,
        legend=True,
        cmap=plot_info['cmap'],  
        linewidth=0.5,
        edgecolor='0.8',
        legend_kwds={'orientation': "horizontal", 'pad': 0.01, 'aspect': 50}
    )
    
    # B. Highlighter Layer (ONLY for Price)
    # We check if we are currently plotting the price column
    if column == 'median_price_per_m2':
        # Filter for rows that were flagged as imputed
        imputed_gdf = latest_year_gdf[latest_year_gdf['is_price_imputed'] == 1]
        
        if not imputed_gdf.empty:
            imputed_gdf.plot(
                ax=ax,
                facecolor='none', 
                edgecolor='black',     # Black border
                linewidth=1.0, 
                hatch='////',        # Hatch pattern
                alpha=0.8
            )
            # Add a text annotation or specialized legend if strictly needed, 
            # but the global legend below handles it.

    ax.set_title(plot_info['title'], fontsize=12) 
    ax.axis('off')

# Custom Legend for the Hatch
patch = mpatches.Patch(facecolor='none', edgecolor='black', hatch='////', label='Interpolated Data')
fig.legend(handles=[patch], loc='upper center', bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 0.93), ncol=1, fontsize=12)

fig.suptitle(f'Socio-Economic Indicators for Barcelona ({target_year})', fontsize=16, y=0.96)
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.92])
plt.show()
In [3]:
def create_animated_map(gdf, column_name, title, cmap='viridis'):
    """
    Creates an animated choropleth map.
    Since Plotly cannot 'hatch' polygons easily, we add the Imputation Status
    to the hover information.
    """
    # 1. Sort for animation
    gdf_sorted = gdf.sort_values(by='year').copy()
    
    # 2. Prepare visual flag for Hover
    # Create a string column: "Observed" vs "Interpolated"
    if 'is_price_imputed' in gdf_sorted.columns and column_name == 'median_price_per_m2':
        gdf_sorted['Data Status'] = gdf_sorted['is_price_imputed'].apply(
            lambda x: "⚠️ INTERPOLATED" if x == 1 else "Observed"
        )
    else:
        gdf_sorted['Data Status'] = "Observed"

    # 3. Determine fixed range
    min_val = gdf_sorted[column_name].min()
    max_val = gdf_sorted[column_name].max()

    # 4. Create Figure
    fig = px.choropleth_map(
        gdf_sorted,
        geojson=gdf_sorted.geometry,
        locations=gdf_sorted.index,
        color=column_name,
        animation_frame="year",
        color_continuous_scale=cmap,
        range_color=[min_val, max_val],
        map_style="carto-positron",
        zoom=11, 
        center={"lat": 41.3851, "lon": 2.1734},
        opacity=0.7,
        title=title,
        # ADD THE STATUS TO HOVER
        hover_data={column_name:':.2f', 'Data Status': True} 
    )

    fig.update_layout(margin={"r":0,"t":40,"l":0,"b":0})
    return fig

# --- Example Usage for Barcelona ---
# Ensure your CRS is 4326 (Lat/Lon) as you did in 
if master_gdf.crs.to_string() != "EPSG:4326":
    master_gdf = master_gdf.to_crs(epsg=4326)

# Animate Median Household Income
fig_bcn_income = create_animated_map(
    master_gdf, 
    column_name='median_rent_per_m2', 
    title='Evolution of Median Rent per m2 in Barcelona (2015-2023)',
    cmap='Viridis'
)
fig_bcn_income.show()

Plotting numerical values on boxplots¶

In [7]:
# --- 1. Load and Prepare the Data ---
master_df = pd.read_csv("../data/preprocessed/barcelona/barcelona_master_dataframe.csv")

# FIX: Convert the string geometry column back to actual polygons
master_df['geometry'] = master_df['geometry'].apply(wkt.loads)

# Create the GeoDataFrame
master_gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(master_df, geometry='geometry', crs='epsg:4326')

# --- 2. Generate and Save Boxplots ---
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
fig_box, axes_box = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 10))
fig_box.suptitle('Distribution of Key Indicators Across All Neighborhoods (Barcelona)', fontsize=16)
axes_box = axes_box.flatten()

# Plot 1: Median Household Income
sns.boxplot(y=master_gdf['median_household_income'], ax=axes_box[0], color='skyblue')
axes_box[0].set_title('Median Household Income (€)')
axes_box[0].set_ylabel('')

# Plot 2: Median Price per m²
sns.boxplot(y=master_gdf['median_price_per_m2'], ax=axes_box[1], color='salmon')
axes_box[1].set_title('Median Cadastral Value (€/m²)')
axes_box[1].set_ylabel('')

# Plot 3: Population Density
sns.boxplot(y=master_gdf['population_density'], ax=axes_box[2], color='lightgreen')
axes_box[2].set_title('Population Density (inhabitants/km²)')
axes_box[2].set_ylabel('')

# Plot 4: Percentage of Young Adults
sns.boxplot(y=master_gdf['pct_young_adults'], ax=axes_box[3], color='gold')
axes_box[3].set_title('Percentage of Young Adults (20-39)')
axes_box[3].set_ylabel('')

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.95])
plt.show()

import matplotlib.patches as mpatches

# --- 1. Load and Prepare Paris Data ---
# Load the CLEAN homogeneous file which has the 'is_interpolated' column
paris_df = pd.read_csv("../data/preprocessed/paris/paris_master_dataframe.csv")
paris_df['geometry'] = paris_df['geometry'].apply(wkt.loads)
paris_gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(paris_df, geometry='geometry', crs='epsg:4326')

# Select a year that has interpolated data (e.g., 2021)
target_year = 2021
latest_paris_gdf = paris_gdf[paris_gdf['year'] == target_year]

# Create a subset for the interpolated neighborhoods
interpolated_gdf = latest_paris_gdf[latest_paris_gdf['is_interpolated'] == True]

print(f"Plotting Year: {target_year}")
print(f"Interpolated Areas Highlighted: {interpolated_gdf['neighborhood_name'].tolist()}")

# --- 2. Create the Grid Plot ---
plots = {
    'median_household_income': {'title': 'Median Household Income (€)', 'cmap': 'viridis'},
    'median_price_per_m2': {'title': 'Median Price (€/m²)', 'cmap': 'plasma'},
    'pct_young_adults': {'title': '% of Young Adults', 'cmap': 'cividis'},
    'population_density': {'title': 'Population Density (pop/km²)', 'cmap': 'inferno'}
}

fig, axes = plt.subplots(nrows=2, ncols=2, figsize=(12, 12))
axes = axes.flatten()

for i, (column, plot_info) in enumerate(plots.items()):
    ax = axes[i]
    
    # 1. Base Plot (All Data)
    latest_paris_gdf.plot(
        column=column,
        ax=ax,
        legend=True,
        cmap=plot_info['cmap'],
        linewidth=0.1,
        edgecolor='0.8',
        legend_kwds={'orientation': "horizontal", 'pad': 0.01, 'aspect': 20}
    )
    
    # 2. Highlighter Layer (Interpolated Areas)
    # We plot them again with NO fill (facecolor='none') but with a red outline and hatch
    if not interpolated_gdf.empty:
        interpolated_gdf.plot(
            ax=ax,
            facecolor='none', 
            edgecolor='red',     # Red border
            linewidth=1.5,       # Thicker line
            hatch='///',         # Striped pattern
            alpha=0.7
        )
    
    ax.set_title(plot_info['title'], fontsize=12)
    ax.axis('off')

# Custom Legend for the Hatch
patch = mpatches.Patch(facecolor='none', edgecolor='red', hatch='///', label='Interpolated Data')
fig.legend(handles=[patch], loc='upper center', bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 0.95), ncol=1, fontsize=12)

fig.suptitle(f'Socio-Economic Indicators for Paris ({target_year})\n(Red areas were spatially interpolated)', fontsize=16, y=0.98)
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.94])
plt.show()

Plotting Year: 2021
Interpolated Areas Highlighted: ["Saint-Germain-l'Auxerrois", 'Gaillon', 'Champs-Elysées']
